value.name: Joe claims entitlement to Rex's money
value.description: Joe asserts that as Mary's husband he would be entitled to Rex's money regardless of what happened to her.
evidence: -- I'm your husband. I'd be entitled to Rex's money. No matter what happened to you.

value.name: Marylin agrees with Joe's claim
value.description: Marylin acknowledges that Joe's statement about entitlement is true.

value.name: Joe insults Marylin and boasts
value.description: Joe declares himself the exterminator and calls Marylin the pestilence in a hostile boast.
evidence: JOE Lemme tell you something. You are the pestilence. I'm the exterminator.

value.name: Marylin offers Joe payment
value.description: Marylin tries to placate Joe by saying she will pay him the twenty thousand.
evidence: MARYLIN Oh Joe, be happy for us. I'll pay you the twenty thousand.

value.name: Miles corrects the payment amount
value.description: Miles interrupts to say the amount owed to Joe was fifty, not twenty, because Joe was charging him the lawyer rate.
evidence: MILES It was fifty for you.
JOE (To Miles) That's cause you're a lawyer. I gave her the lawyer discount.

value.name: Joe insults Marylin as a whore
value.description: Joe escalates the confrontation by calling Marylin a whore who worships money.
evidence: But I shouldn't of. Cause you're a whore. A whore who worships the dollar.

value.name: Marylin jokes about whores worshipping money
value.description: Marylin responds with a sardonic joke that all whores worship the dollar.
evidence: MARYLIN Well, actually, all whores worship the dollar, if you want to get technical.

value.name: Joe reveals his former legal career
value.description: Joe says he used to be a lawyer like Miles and that his clients were whores like Marylin.
evidence: I was a lawyer. Just like you. And my clients? Whores just like you.

value.name: Miles recognizes Joe as Kaplan lawyer
value.description: Miles realizes Joe is Joe Gittelson, a lawyer he studied and admired from Kaplan.
evidence: MILES Were you with a firm?
MILES Kaplan? I know Kaplan. Wait. You're Joe Gittelson? I knew you looked -- You were great -- we studied you.

value.name: Joe explains his disillusionment with matrimonial law
value.description: Joe says twenty years in matrimonial law made him sick and led to an epiphany about clients wanting revenge.
evidence: Twenty years in "matrimonial law" and it made me sick.
I broke up homes and families, never givin' it a second thought. Till one day. I had an epiphany.

value.name: Joe describes his violent legal philosophy
value.description: Joe concludes that clients want their exes dead and that the best service to them is to kill them.
evidence: Joe -- everyone you see wants blood. Everyone wants their ex's dead. So why jerk around with rest. You wanna best serve your clients? Kill em.
